g.text: Events write typed tags onto each chunk; corrective retrieval filters, grades and corrects on them; what fails grading becomes the next round of tags.
1 · EVENTS WRITE THE TAGS (NO TAGGING PROJECT)
Organic search in BigQuery matches a doc
Freshness(Timestamp), // when it was last true
A typo, renamed campaign or expired consent
can't pass as a valid tag: the compiler rejects
2 · CRAG USES THE TAGS AT EVERY STEP
Vector query searches only chunks whose Market,
Locale and Sensitivity match the request.
A KR shopper never retrieves a GB-only promotion.
Ambiguous: re-query with tags relaxed one level
Fail: decline and escalate to a person, with the
Low-confidence and declined questions are logged
That log feeds BigQuery audiences and de-
identified LoRA training pairs: the next round of
organic loop: failures become new tags
The chunk owns its tags. Revoking consent removes
Consent from the chunk itself: no stale copy left
in a spreadsheet or a plugin cache.
Add a Tag variant and the build breaks until every
grader handles it. A new rule can't be silently
3 to 10 tags per chunk: a linear scan of a small
Vec beats a hash map, and it serialises straight
into vector-store metadata for the pre-filter.
Free-text strings like "uk-promo-2024" set by a
consultant. Nothing checks them, nothing expires
them, and the chatbot retrieves them anyway.
4 · WHY RUST IN E-COMMERCE, CONSENT, SECURITY AND DATA LOAD
Price, stock and order state are typed values, not
strings: a Money(amount, ISO 4217) can't be added
to a different currency by accident.
Idempotency keys are a type, so a retried checkout
Consent is an owned value with a scope and an
expiry. Withdrawal drops it, and every path that
needs it fails to compile without a check.
source: business (a default) and source: platform
Memory safety removes the buffer overflows and
use-after-free bugs behind about 70% of serious C
Keys are generated from a secure random source,
zeroised on drop, and never copied into logs or
Streams large feeds, catalogs and event logs with
Parse once into types at the boundary; bad rows
are rejected at load, not discovered by AI at
5 · EVERY THEME LOADS THROUGH THE CLOUDFLARE HELMET, REGARDLESS OF CMS PUBLISH
The CMS publish owns presentation only
vanilla HTML · CSS · JS · petite-vue · HTMX
No React bundle, no theme API: any template carries it. No theme, plugin or
Xano release gate · source of truth
Consent at the system of record
Async Rust GET / POST / PATCH / DELETE from any stack: Tokio + reqwest or
worker::Fetch. Vectorize, caches and feeds are derived copies.
6 · SHOPIFY PRODUCT GRAPHQL TO VERTEX AI AND CRAG, JOINED BY THE SHOPIFY GID
or missing GTIN is rejected at
Price and stock fetched live at
live GraphQL call for price and stock at answer time: a vector store holding last night's price is how a chatbot quotes a wrong price

Also: Shopify → BigQuery export feeds Vertex AI audiences and LoRA pairs, gated by consent. Merchant Center → Vertex AI Search for commerce shares the GTIN/MPN identities but does not grade against your consent and provenance tags.
7 · HEAP VS STACK, AND BIT LENGTH: WHERE KEY MATERIAL LIVES
Fixed size: u64, bool, [u8; 32], a struct's own
Size known at runtime: String text, Vec items, BigUint limbs
title: String · tags: Vec<Tag> · variants: Vec<Variant>
Reserved and released as the function returns
Allocated, followed through a pointer, freed on drop
Fixed-size key: one place in memory; zeroise on
A growing Vec can reallocate and leave old copies behind
Why bit length matters for the eMudhra issue, and why it isn't enough

A longer key resists brute force; it doesn't help once the key itself is taken. The October 2026 intermediate was compromised, not cracked. What protects you: short-lived keys, HSM custody, fixed-size keys zeroised on drop, and a trust store you can distrust.
